flags: FHWA describes a 48-mile byway; material maps 45.3 miles. BLM separately describes seven-mile and twelve-mile approaches from Beaver and Carlton. The cache does not resolve those measurement boundaries, so 48 miles is attributed to FHWA rather than equated with the catalog geometry.

No cache page supplies the road’s construction history, designation date or campaign. The middle overview paragraph uses documented geology and the timber-producing landscape instead of inventing a road-origin narrative.

The Carlton cache contains a garbled diary sentence and contradicts itself on the town’s namesake. Omitted the disputed name derivation, diary and unverified former-post-office access. The current seven-mile distance is restored to the source’s qualification, about seven miles.

The current unconditional Alder Glen Falls view is narrowed to the documented seasonal photo captions; no year-round visibility or campground opening is promised. BLM says camping is generally May–October, distinct from the year-round road.

Dropped the current Beaver naming explanation as a town-specific assertion: its cache discusses regional beaver place-names and pioneer associations without explicitly establishing this community’s naming. Changed the current rainfall hedge to the unhedged 120 inches stated by FHWA.
Practical checked date is the requested cache-review date, not a claim of live road-condition verification.

The overview is shorter than 200 words because the cache supplies little route history or detailed driving character beyond the canyon and approaches. Beaver and Alder Glen remain short because their place-specific evidence is thin; Carlton’s account is concise because the historical extract is internally inconsistent and partly garbled.
